data.text/markdown:
SAFT-VR-CS: helium / hydrogen mixtures

Test of the SAFT-VR-CS combining rules for the effective (corresponding-states) parameters.
  1. Pure helium and hydrogen with the Ziegler parameters (parameters/saftvrcs/saft_vr_cs_params.json) vs. NIST.
  2. He/H||(_2||) mixture with two routes to the unlike parameters, vs. experimental data (DDB) and GEMC:
    • effective: combine the effective pure-component parameters (each at its own mass) with the SAFT-VR Mie rules.
    • classical: combine the classical parameters with the SAFT-VR Mie rules, then map the pair at the pair mass ||(m_{ij} = 2 m_i m_j / (m_i + m_j)||) with prefactors ||(\zeta_{ij} = (\zeta_i + \zeta_j)/2||).

data.text/markdown:
Effective parameters in SAFT-VR-CS

Every component is mapped onto a classical Mie potential with temperature-dependent effective parameters ||(\sigma_\mathrm{eff}||), ||(\varepsilon_\mathrm{eff}||), ||(\lambda_{r,\mathrm{eff}}||); the attractive exponent stays ||(\lambda_a = 6||). The hard-sphere diameter (Barker-Henderson), the Mie prefactor ||(C||) and the dispersion terms of SAFT-VR Mie are evaluated with these effective parameters.

Like pairs (||(ii||))

Reduced quantum parameter with the particle mass ||(m_i||) (segment number ||(= 1||)): ||[D^*_i = \frac{\hbar^2}{12\, m_i\, k_\mathrm{B} T\, \sigma_i^2}||]||[\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{eff},i}}{\sigma_i} = F^\sigma\!\left(D^*_i, \lambda_{r,i}; \zeta^\sigma_i\right), \qquad \frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff},i}}{\varepsilon_i} = F^\varepsilon\!\left(D^*_i, \lambda_{r,i}; \zeta^\varepsilon_i\right), \qquad \frac{\lambda_{r,\mathrm{eff},i}}{\lambda_{r,i}} = F^\lambda\!\left(D^*_i, \lambda_{r,i}; \zeta^\lambda_i\right)||]with (||(X = \sigma, \varepsilon||); coefficients ||(c^X_k(\lambda_r) = a^X_k + b^X_k \lambda_r + d^X_k \lambda_r^2||)) ||[F^X = \frac{1 + \zeta^X_0 c^X_0 D^* + \zeta^X_1 c^X_1 D^{*2} + \zeta^X_3 D^{*3}}{1 + \zeta^X_2 c^X_2 D^* + \zeta^X_4 D^{*2}}, \qquad F^\lambda = \frac{1 + \zeta^\lambda_0 c^\lambda_0 D^* + \zeta^\lambda_1 c^\lambda_1 D^{*2} + \zeta^\lambda_2 c^\lambda_2 D^{*3}}{1 + \zeta^\lambda_3 c^\lambda_3 D^* + \zeta^\lambda_4 c^\lambda_4 D^{*2}}||]The ||(\zeta||) are the component-specific prefactors (Csigma k, Ceps k, Crep k in the parameter file). Defaults: ||(\zeta^{\sigma,\varepsilon} = (1, 1, 1, 0, 0)||), ||(\zeta^\lambda = (1, 1, 1, 1, 1)||).

Unlike pairs (||(ij||)), route effective

SAFT-VR Mie combining rules applied to the effective pure-component parameters (each at its own mass ||(m_i||)): ||[\sigma_{\mathrm{eff},ij} = \frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{eff},i} + \sigma_{\mathrm{eff},j}}{2}, \qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff},ij} = (1 - k_{ij}) \frac{\sqrt{\sigma_{\mathrm{eff},i}^3 \sigma_{\mathrm{eff},j}^3}}{\sigma_{\mathrm{eff},ij}^3} \sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff},i}\, \varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff},j}}, \qquad \lambda_{r,\mathrm{eff},ij} = 3 + (1 - \gamma_{ij}) \sqrt{(\lambda_{r,\mathrm{eff},i} - 3)(\lambda_{r,\mathrm{eff},j} - 3)}||]

Unlike pairs (||(ij||)), route classical

  1. SAFT-VR Mie combining rules applied to the classical parameters:
||[\sigma_{ij} = \frac{\sigma_i + \sigma_j}{2}, \qquad \varepsilon_{ij} = (1 - k_{ij}) \frac{\sqrt{\sigma_i^3 \sigma_j^3}}{\sigma_{ij}^3} \sqrt{\varepsilon_i \varepsilon_j}, \qquad \lambda_{r,ij} = 3 + (1 - \gamma_{ij}) \sqrt{(\lambda_{r,i} - 3)(\lambda_{r,j} - 3)}||]
  1. Mapping of the pair with the pair mass (harmonic mean, i.e. the reduced mass of the Feynman-Hibbs correction) and the mean prefactors:
||[m_{ij} = \frac{2 m_i m_j}{m_i + m_j}, \qquad D^*_{ij} = \frac{\hbar^2}{12\, m_{ij}\, k_\mathrm{B} T\, \sigma_{ij}^2}, \qquad \zeta_{ij} = \frac{\zeta_i + \zeta_j}{2}||]||[\sigma_{\mathrm{eff},ij} = \sigma_{ij} F^\sigma\!\left(D^*_{ij}, \lambda_{r,ij}; \zeta^\sigma_{ij}\right), \qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff},ij} = \varepsilon_{ij} F^\varepsilon\!\left(D^*_{ij}, \lambda_{r,ij}; \zeta^\varepsilon_{ij}\right), \qquad \lambda_{r,\mathrm{eff},ij} = \lambda_{r,ij} F^\lambda\!\left(D^*_{ij}, \lambda_{r,ij}; \zeta^\lambda_{ij}\right)||]For ||(i = j||) both routes reduce to the like-pair equations.

data.text/markdown:
Fit of ||(k_{ij}||) for the classical route

Objective: AARD of the bubble pressures at the experimental ||((T, x_\mathrm{He})||) (DDB, all references); points without a converged bubble point count as 100 %. A scan showed the minimum between ||(k_{ij} = 0.25||) and ||(0.3||); for ||(k_{ij} \gtrsim 0.33||) single points diverge.
||(k_{ij}||) = 0.2568, objective 40.7 % (11 evaluations)

Models in the comparison

model binary parameters
SAFT-VR-CS, effective ||(k_{ij} = \gamma_{ij} = 0||) predictive
SAFT-VR-CS, classical ||(k_{ij} = \gamma_{ij} = 0||) predictive
SAFT-VR-CS, classical, fitted ||(k_{ij}||) ||(k_{ij}||) fitted above, ||(\gamma_{ij} = 0||) 1 binary parameter
SAFT-VRQ Mie, ||(k_{ij} = l_{ij} = 0||) none predictive
SAFT-VRQ Mie (Aasen 2020) ||(k_{ij} = 0.08||), ||(l_{ij} = -0.05||) 2 binary parameters
SAFT-VRQ Mie applies the Feynman-Hibbs correction directly to the unlike pair (reduced mass, combined classical ||(\sigma_{ij}||), ||(\varepsilon_{ij}||), ||(\lambda_{ij}||)), which corresponds to the classical route of SAFT-VR-CS. Its ||(l_{ij}||) acts on ||(\sigma_{ij}||); SAFT-VR-CS has no ||(l_{ij}||) (only ||(k_{ij}||) and ||(\gamma_{ij}||) on ||(\lambda_{r,ij}||)). Only the predictive rows compare the models on equal terms; the fitted rows show what one or two binary parameters achieve.

data.text/html: Converged of 667 points: SAFT-VR-CS, effective: 518, SAFT-VR-CS, classical: 521, SAFT-VR-CS, classical, ||(k_{ij}||) = 0.257: 622, SAFT-VRQ Mie, ||(k_{ij} = l_{ij} = 0||): 526, SAFT-VRQ Mie (Aasen 2020): 595; all models: 473. Dew points above the model's mixture critical pressure have no solution.

data.text/markdown:
Findings (2026-10-20)

Pure fluids (vs. NIST): SAFT-VR-CS with the Ziegler parameters reproduces ||(p_\mathrm{sat}||) within about 2 % and ||(\rho_l||) within 1 % (AARD) for both helium and hydrogen; larger deviations only close to ||(T_c||). SAFT-VRQ Mie (Aasen 2019) is clearly worse for helium (AARD ||(p_\mathrm{sat}||) 37 %), similar for hydrogen (6 %). Mixture, predictive (||(k_{ij} = 0||); AARD ||(p||) on the 473 data points where all models converge):
  • SAFT-VR-CS effective 62.6 %, classical 61.3 %, SAFT-VRQ Mie (||(k_{ij} = l_{ij} = 0||)) 55.9 %.
  • All predictive models dissolve far too much helium in liquid hydrogen (bubble pressures too low).
  • The classical route raises the bubble pressures compared to effective; the effect is large near the mixture critical region at low ||(T||) (15.5 K, 17.4 K) but small on the data points, most of which are at low ||(x_\mathrm{He}||). It moves SAFT-VR-CS towards SAFT-VRQ Mie, which treats the unlike pair in the same way.
Mixture, fitted binary parameters:
  • SAFT-VR-CS classical with fitted ||(k_{ij} = 0.257||): AARD ||(p||) 36.6 %, AAD of the coexisting composition 0.047.
  • SAFT-VRQ Mie (Aasen 2020, ||(k_{ij} = 0.08||), ||(l_{ij} = -0.05||)): AARD ||(p||) 28.7 %, 0.034.
  • The fitted ||(k_{ij}||) of SAFT-VR-CS is much larger than that of SAFT-VRQ Mie. One candidate reason (not checked): the Ziegler helium ||(\varepsilon/k_\mathrm{B} = 9.56||) K is much larger than Aasen's 5.42 K, so the geometric-mean unlike energy starts higher. With ||(k_{ij} = 0.257||) the two-phase region opens up at high pressure (no closed loop below 200 bar at ||(T \le 29||) K) and is too wide at 27.8 K and 31.5 K; a single ||(k_{ij}||) cannot match low and high temperatures at the same time.
